candidates.source_body_excerpt: One of the borough's leading sports clubs joins forces with the town's professional football team to widen access to physical activity Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and Rochdale Netball Club are delighted to announce the launch of Rochdale AFC Netball. The agreement will see Rochdale Netball Club rebrand and become part of the club's wider 'Our Teams' family. The partnership brings together one of the borough's leading community sports clubs with its professional football club and official charitable arm, creating a stronger platform to grow netball and widen access to physical activity across Rochdale — from primary school participation through to junior and adult club netball, coaching, volunteering and leadership. Netball is one of the most widely played team sports in England, particularly among women and girls, with accessible formats for all ages and abilities, including junior netball, Back to Netball and Walking Netball. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the partnership will raise the sport's profile locally, strengthen school-to-club links, and give more people a clear route into the game. Currently, Rochdale Netball Club runs teams from under-sixes right through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court every week. The agreement will also support wider community outcomes, with Rochdale AFC Community Trust working alongside Rochdale AFC Netball on new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing, and volunteer development. Operating under a shared Rochdale AFC identity opens up new opportunities too, from commercial support and matchday promotion to community events and sponsorship, reinforcing that women's sport has a central place in the borough's sporting future. The move follows a model seen elsewhere in professional sport, where football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to boost visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the priority will be a community-first approach that reflects the town's sporting pride and welcomes people of all ages.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale’s largest housing estate is about to get even bigger now plans for more homes have been approved. The Kirkholt estate will get a new 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses off Queen’s Drive. The developer, Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), says all the homes would be available for social rent (around 60 per cent of market rates). The idea behind this scheme is to bring ‘much-needed’ affordable housing to the area. Click here for the latest on Greater Manchester's politics in our newsletter MSV is a not-for-profit Registered Provider who own and manage almost 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire and West Yorkshire. The apartments would all be one-beds and the terraced homes would contain four-bedrooms each. The site where the homes will be built currently sits empty. An old block of flats used to sit on the land next to the A664 (Queensway), but it was demolished in 2009. It was used as a temporary space by Kirkholt Medical Practice for a short time before the health centre got its permanent digs down the road. Planning papers read: “The application site is a prominent site within the local area. The intention is to create a high-quality sustainable development that addresses housing needs and meets the needs of the local community. “This proposal has been developed in response to an identified local demand, helping to reduce anti-social behaviour issues and the various problems associated with the site in its disused state. “By redeveloping the former brownfield site, we plan on increasing the benefits of its regeneration by utilising vacant land and delivering affordable homes for local residents. “MSV’s vision for this site is to create a secure outward looking scheme for social rent. They want to provide housing, with the aim of creating a balanced community and to promote tenure diversification in the area.” Plans for a new community garden, to compliment the scheme, were also approved last month. It would be run by Q Gardens, a community group that already operates in the Kirkholt area.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Pakistan has warned that its cooperation with the United Kingdom (UK) on the return of illegal migrants could be affected if London continues to pressure Islamabad to accept convicted child sex offender Shabir Ahmed, a British newspaper has reported. Senior Pakistani government officials told the news outlet that Islamabad had maintained close cooperation with Britain by facilitating the return of rejected asylum seekers, visa overstayers and immigration offenders. However, they said that the UK’s insistence on deporting Ahmed to Pakistan after his release from prison could damage existing agreements on migrant returns and affect broader cooperation on intelligence, security and organised crime. Pakistani officials also expressed concern over reports suggesting that Britain could impose measures such as visa restrictions on Pakistani nationals and reductions in foreign aid if Islamabad continued to reject Ahmed’s return. British authorities are seeking to increase the deportation of foreign offenders to ease pressure on overcrowded prisons. Official figures show that 306 Pakistani nationals are being held in UK prisons as of June 30. Ahmed was released from prison last month after serving 14 years of a 22-year sentence for multiple child rape convictions. British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced plans to amend immigration laws to remove a legal barrier that prevented the Home Office from deporting Ahmed after his British citizenship was revoked. Pakistan has refused to accept Ahmed, arguing that he renounced his Pakistani citizenship and has spent most of his life in Britain.

The Kirkholt estate will get a new 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses off Queen’s Drive. The developer, Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), says all the homes would be available for social rent (around 60 per cent of market rates).

The idea behind this scheme is to bring ‘much-needed’ affordable housing to the area.

MSV is a not-for-profit Registered Provider who own and manage almost 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire and West Yorkshire. 

The apartments would all be one-beds and the terraced homes would contain four-bedrooms each.

The site where the homes will be built currently sits empty. An old block of flats used to sit on the land next to the A664 (Queensway), but it was demolished in 2009. 

It was used as a temporary space by Kirkholt Medical Practice for a short time before the health centre got its permanent digs down the road.

Planning papers read: “The application site is a prominent site within the local area. The intention is to create a high-quality sustainable development that addresses housing needs and meets the needs of the local community.

“This proposal has been developed in response to an identified local demand, helping to reduce anti-social behaviour issues and the various problems associated with the site in its disused state.

“By redeveloping the former brownfield site, we plan on increasing the benefits of its regeneration by utilising vacant land and delivering affordable homes for local residents.

“MSV’s vision for this site is to create a secure outward looking scheme for social rent. They want to provide housing, with the aim of creating a balanced community and to promote tenure diversification in the area.”

Plans for a new community garden, to compliment the scheme, were also approved last month. It would be run by Q Gardens, a community group that already operates in the Kirkholt area.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: US actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. A representative for the actress confirmed the death to US network ABC News on Sunday, saying her family would remember her “incredible light” who brought “immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her”. The statement from her father Skip read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.” Her father also asked that her family be given privacy as they “take time to process this unimaginable loss”. No cause of death has been announced. The 36-year-old began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas before gaining wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember The Titans alongside Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in 1998’s A Bug’s Life. Panettiere later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before going on to star as up-and-coming country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on the hit TV series Nashville. Her film credits include 2006’s Bring It On: All Or Nothing, comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed. Following her rapid rise to fame, the pressure of the industry began to weigh on Panettiere – with the actress previously revealing that she had struggled with addiction throughout her 20s. In a memoir published earlier this year, Panettiere opened up about her struggles with mental health, the loss of her younger brother, Jansen, and her decision to give full custody of her daughter to her former partner, Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko.

Hornets made a strong start, and led 6-0, but were then 14-6 behind before mounting their own comeback. When Town were penalised early on, Max Flanagan slotted the goal, and his side extended their advantage after ten minutes when Harvey Braddish was hauled down by the line and Ross Whitmore dived in from dummy-half. Flanagan was unable to convert. The visitors were having much the better of the contest for the first 25 minutes with Mark Ioane, Jordan Syme and Chris Barratt enjoying their forays at the Workington pack. With some handling errors added to the mix, the hosts found themselves in a midfield slog. But they gradually began to turn the screw and were unfortunate with two chances. The first came after half an hour when Evan Lawther brushed away from two defenders on the left and went to Oscar Doran, who sped into the backfield, but with the support of debutant Jaiden Tallantire and Jake Carter inside, the pass went between both players. Then a wonderful pass from Tallantire undid Rochdale on the right – but Zarrin Galea couldn’t take the ball cleanly.

First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge and Dale’s return to the fourth tier went from bad to worse when left-back Bryant Bilongo was shown a second yellow card midway through the second half before Yahya Bamba made it 3-0 in stoppage time. We’ve got to be more aggressive in what we do out of possession and we applied pressure in the right areas. I’m really pleased with the performance.” It was a different story for Rochdale boss Ian Watson, who replaced promotion-winning manger Jimmy McNulty after he departed for Stockport County during the summer. “It was not good,” admitted Watson. “It’s a tough moment for us, for sure. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Newport and new manager Hayden Mullins enjoyed a dream start to their League Two campaign with a 3-0 home win over newly-promoted Rochdale. First-half goals from summer signings Kyle Cameron and Shaquille Gwengwe put the Exiles in charge at a sun-baked Rodney Parade. Dale’s return to the fourth tier went from bad to worse when left-back Bryant Bilongo was shown a second yellow card for upending Cameron Norman in the 66th minute before Yahya Bamba added County’s third late on. Both teams started slowly, but it was the hosts who kicked into gear first and they opened their account for the league season in the 18th minute when captain Cameron poked in from close range after Bamba had headed on a Harrison Biggins corner. Ciaran Brennan and Christian Doidge were both denied by Rochdale goalkeeper Nils Ramming before Gwengwe nipped in front of the Brighton loanee to stab in a second from Biggins’ cross. Any hopes of a Rochdale fightback were ended by Bilongo’s dismissal and Bamba lashed in a third in stoppage time to add to their misery.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's column with Mayor of Rochdale, councillor Faisal Rana It is two months since I had the great honour of becoming Mayor of Rochdale. It is a huge privilege to serve the community, along with my wife, Mayoress of Rochdale Iram Faisal. Since May we have already visited hundreds of charities, schools, businesses and events in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale. We have been humbled by the generosity and kindness of people across the borough, it’s been a truly inspiring start to the Mayoral year. As well as so many delightful visits, I think it’s really important to showcase the best of our borough to a national and international audiences. We have such a good story to tell about our borough I am really keen, throughout my mayoral year, to spread the positive messages as wide as possible. It’s in that spirit that, over recent weeks, visitors to the Mayor’s Parlour have included international friends such as the Consulate General of China, the Consulate General of Italy and the Consulate General of Spain. The international flavour was complemented by other lovely visits, including the Assistant High Commissioner of Bangladesh. These distinguished guests really enjoyed their visits, and were particularly impressed by our stunning Grade 1 Rochdale Town Hall. It was an absolute honour and pleasure to meet them. It’s in that international spirit of cooperation, in the true Rochdalian way, that we have such strong relationships with our twin towns and cities. As part of that ongoing and lasting link, I was delighted to welcome the Friends of Tourcoing to the town hall. Rochdale has been formally twinned with the French City since 1956, a long and heartfelt bond of love. We enjoyed afternoon tea and took a trip down memory lane, as well as toasting many more years of friendship. The past pointing the way to an even better future. Many thanks for such a lovely visit. When I became Mayor of Rochdale I gave a commitment to visit all parts of the borough and over the last few weeks I have attended events across all townships. These have included Love Littleborough, Heywood Community Fun Day, MiddFest and a lovely and well attended Rochdale Pride. It was lovely to see so many of you at these important events, showing our borough’s diversity and inclusivity at its very best. As a former veteran, with many years’ service in the Pakistan Navy, I have a strong connection with our local Armed Forces community. I am very proud to have the Armed Forces Breakfast Club as one of mayoral charities. Key forces events I have recently attended include Armed Forces Day flag raisings at Rochdale Town Hall and Middleton Memorial Gardens, Minden Day flag raising and regular visits to the breakfast club. Our local veterans’ community really do represent the very best of us. I was also extremely proud and humbled to award Wing Commander David Forbes with a special mayoral certificate. David has been at the heart of the local armed forces community for many years, serving with great distinction as president of the Rochdale branch of the Royal British Legion. He’s been at the heart of many local initiatives that have grown and expanded over the years, including the breakfast club. There is no one more deserving of mayoral recognition than David. Other key events I have attended over recent weeks have included a charming summer garden celebration at Springhill Hospice; as I said in my last column Springhill is an incredible organisation, caring for patients and loved ones across the borough of Rochdale who are affected by life limiting conditions like cancer, motor neurone disease, and heart failure. We are blessed to have this in incredible organisation in our borough and long may they continue to make every moment count.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Visitors were treated to priceless masterpieces, family workshops, and free Warhol-inspired ice cream Rochdale Town Hall Square was given a vibrant, pop-art makeover as original masterpieces by legendary artist Andy Warhol rolled into town-housed inside a specialist fine art transport vehicle. The unique, one-day-only mobile exhibition brought world-famous artwork out of traditional gallery walls and directly into the heart of the community. Locals visiting the town's Side by Side festival were able to step inside the truck to view iconic pieces up close, including Warhol’s famous Self-Portrait with Skull (1978) and Self-Portrait with Platinum Bouffant Wig (1981). Organised by cultural charity Your Trust in partnership with ARTIST ROOMS (Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland), the surprise display turned the square into an outdoor creative hub. The pop-up event serves as a teaser for an even bigger partnership planned for 2027, when the newly re-developed Touchstones gallery reopens its doors. Mark Doyle, director of Arts, Heritage and Wellness at Your Trust/Touchstones Rochdale, said: "This is a fantastic opportunity for the people across Rochdale Borough to experience world-renowned art right on their doorstep.
